title: BROWSEREXPORT1 slice png-sequence reference (3 frames, unit/helper delivery)

environment.dependencies: npm ci in the worktree (22 packages)
environment.prerequisite: public/fem-kernel.wasm built with node scripts/build-kernel.mjs (same prerequisite as npm test); public/cad and public/gmsh were not needed for this box solve
environment.browser: No desktop browser was connected to this session (browser.tabs.list returned [browser.disconnected]); no studio MCP pairing was attempted. No real-Chrome verification was run.

scope.runtime: none (no source change; no reproduced blocking defect in the slice path)

referenceInput.kind: real headless solve, not a synthetic result
referenceInput.conditions: fixed +Z face at z=0; force 100 N in +Z on the z=40 face
referenceInput.solver: analyzeProject (scripts/headless-analysis.mjs), elastic, options {size:5, method:'wasm-pcg', adaptive:false, maxRounds:3}, default worker isolation
referenceInput.mesh: volume mesh; coordinate ranges measured by the test: X 0..10 mm, Y 0..10 mm, Z 0..40 mm

commands.result: passed: tests 30, pass 30, fail 0, cancelled 0, skipped 0 (new file 7, pre-existing 23; baseline of the two pre-existing files was 23 pass / 0 fail before the change)

checks.detail: fixedFrameSchedule({animation:'slice',frames:3,state:animationState,min:0,max:10}) gives index 0/1/2, phase 0/0.5/1 and slicePosition 0/5/10 (mm). Repeated calls are deep-equal (pure). animationState slice at phase 0/0.5/1 with min 2 max 6 gives 2/4/6.

The 0..10 mm X range equals the solved volume mesh node extremes (X 0..10, Y 0..10, Z 0..40), i.e. the range comes from the solved mesh on the selected clip axis, not a UI default. Built-in coordinates are documented as mm in src/project-import.js.

render({format:'png-sequence',animation:'slice',frames:3}) returns application/zip. Independent STORE reader sees exactly manifest.json + frame-0000..0002.png; central and local method are 0; per-entry CRC-32 recomputed from the bytes matches; local offsets are contiguous. Manifest: kind airpocket-fixed-frame-png-sequence, animation slice, frameCount 3, schemaVersion 1, resultRevision recorded, resolution {width:320,height:316} (the test canvas 320x200 + 116 caption band), schedule phase 'index/(frameCount-1)', timeBasis 'frame index', realtime false, wallClockIndependent true, per-frame phase 0/0.5/1 and slicePosition 0/5/10.
A recording renderer observed clip-position 0/5/10 for the three captured frames while clip-enabled was true and clip-axis stayed 0, matching manifest.frames[].slicePosition exactly.

Each frame entry's sha256 matches node:crypto SHA-256 of the ZIP data; frame.bytes equals the stored size; each frame parses as PNG signature + IHDR with a valid IHDR CRC and reports 320x316, equal to manifest.resolution. The three frames have three distinct SHA-256 values and three distinct payloads. NOTE: the frame bytes are produced by the test double's PNG encoder, not by a browser canvas rasteriser; distinct frames only prove per-frame state is carried, not section-physics accuracy.

Two exports from the same frozen result and locale produced byte-identical ZIPs. Condition recorded: caption/locale text is drawn into the canvas by the real capture() but the test double draws no text, so bytes can differ in a real browser when locale or captions change; determinism here is scoped to identical frozen view/locale/result (and to schemaVersion 1 resultRevision, which embeds wall-clock solveMs, so a fresh solve changes the bytes unless physicalRevision is used).
With clip-axis 2 the same 3-frame export produced slicePosition and observed clip-position 0/20/40 mm, showing the range follows the selected axis (Z 0..40 mm) rather than a fixed X range.

createVisualExportJobs: png-sequence with seconds is refused ('png-sequence is fixed-frame; seconds is not accepted, use frames'); frames 1 is refused; the completed job artifact is application/zip, frameCount 3, container zip, compression store, time.animation slice, time.frameSelection 'deterministic schedule', resolution 320x316. Reassembled artifact pages hash to artifact.sha256 and the inner manifest.json entry hash/size match. A result without a volume mesh fails the job with 'Generate a volume mesh first.' and the artifact is unavailable with 0 frames rendered.

Cancelling the slice job after the first frame settles as cancelled, artifact() throws 'Visual export artifact is unavailable', exactly 1 frame was captured (no partial ZIP), and clip-position (4), clip-enabled (false), controls.enabled/enableDamping and isActive were restored. Verified only through the job/adapter layer in Node, not in a real browser.

FIXED_FRAME_LIMITS is still {minFrames:2,maxFrames:120,defaultFrames:24,maxFrameBytes:4 MiB,maxTotalBytes:24 MiB} and FIXED_FRAME_ANIMATIONS is still orbit/deformation/time/slice. No limit was loosened and no ZIP/CRC/physicalRevision mechanism was reimplemented.

observationsNotFixed.detail: src/visual-export.js renderSequence computes min/max with Math.min(...coordinates)/Math.max(...coordinates) over the clip-axis coordinates. Measured with Node v24.11.1: 65536 and 100000 arguments are accepted, 125000 throws RangeError 'Maximum call stack size exceeded'. A mesh with roughly 125000 or more nodes on the export path would therefore fail png-sequence export instead of exporting or refusing explicitly. Reproduced only with synthetic arrays of numbers, not with a real mesh solve, and not fixed here: it is a runtime change outside the small slice-reference delivery and is reported for a separate minimal fix plus regression test.

The in-ZIP manifest records frames[].slicePosition but no per-frame unit label for the section position; mm is implied by the project geometry (built-in coordinates and display units are mm). No runtime change was made because nothing is ambiguous in the tested scenarios, but it is a documentation gap worth a follow-up if API consumers read slicePosition without project units.
